Default since the [GHSA-vg6x-rcgg-rjx6](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/security/advisories/GHSA-vg6x-rcgg-rjx6) fix (4.5.6/5.4.12/6.0.9); every Vite 7.x/8.x release enforces it. List the proxy's hostnames explicitly -- `allowedHosts: ['.ddev.site']` (a leading dot allows the domain and every subdomain) plus any `additional_fqdns` -- and allow the same origins in `cors` (default: localhost only); `cors` controls cross-origin loading, not the 403. Never use `allowedHosts: true` or `cors: true`: both let any website read the dev server's sources. Set the options **inside the single existing `server:` block** -- a second `server: { ... }` literal silently overwrites the first's keys without warning. See `references/vite-configuration.md`.

findings.message: Skill instructs the agent to omit warnings, disclaimers, or ethical commentary. Stripping safety caveats hides risk from the user and is a common jailbreak preamble.
findings.remediation: Remove instructions that suppress warnings, disclaimers, or ethical commentary. Let the agent surface safety-relevant caveats to the user.

findings.code_snippet:
> **Anti-pattern: duplicate `server:` blocks.** Define `server:` exactly once in
> `defineConfig({ ... })`. JavaScript object literals **silently overwrite**
> earlier keys with later ones, so two `server: { ... }` blocks lose the first
> one's options without warning. If you add `allowedHosts`, put it inside the
> existing `server` block — do not create a second one.
>
> **Not a version-specific quirk.** Host-header enforcement isn't a 7.x
